idfDar.description: The International Diabetes Federation and the DAR International Alliance published this score in 2021 to estimate the risk of fasting during Ramadan.

idfDar.otherFasts: The IDF-DAR score was designed for Ramadan. Rozmarra applies it to other fasts as an approximation.

layers.title: How Rozmarra makes its estimates
layers.score: The IDF-DAR 2021 risk score gives the standard clinical score for the risk of fasting. Rozmarra calculates it from the health record and the fasting plan.
layers.twin: The physiology twin is a model of glucose, insulin, meals and medicines for one patient. It shows how a fasting plan may change the patient's glucose, with a band that shows the uncertainty.
layers.model: The prediction model combines the twin's forecast with the recent glucose readings, the smartwatch data and the health record. It estimates the chance of low blood sugar within the next 60 minutes and the chance of high blood sugar after the fast. A short list of reasons explains each estimate.
layers.doctor: Rozmarra supports the doctor. It never changes medicines by itself, and it never judges the decision to fast.

data.name: Data source

testing.title: How the team tested Rozmarra
testing.real: Real normal days: the team tested the model on held-out days of {{patients}} real patients from ShanghaiT2DM and CGMacros, with five-fold cross-validation grouped by person. These days contain no fasts.
testing.synthetic: Simulated fasting days: the team created {{patients}} virtual patients with {{episodes}} fasting days. The model learned from the training group and was tested on {{test}} virtual patients that it had never seen.
testing.baselines: The team compared the model with simpler methods: the last glucose value, a straight-line trend, the twin alone, the IDF-DAR score alone and a model that uses only CGM data.
testing.intervals: The 95% intervals come from bootstrapping by patient.

results.title: Results and targets
results.description: The targets come from the product requirements. The team reports every measured value, including the values that fall short of a target.
results.caption: AUROC shows how well a method separates the moments before an event from other moments. A value of 1 is perfect, and a value of 0.5 is the same as guessing.
results.e1Real: Low blood sugar within 60 minutes, real normal days (AUROC)
results.e1Synthetic: Low blood sugar within 60 minutes, simulated fasting days (AUROC)
results.detected: Share of low blood sugar events detected in time, simulated fasting days
results.falseAlerts: False alerts per patient per fasting day, simulated fasting days
results.warning: Median warning time before low blood sugar, simulated fasting days
results.e2: High blood sugar after the fast is broken, simulated fasting days (AUROC)
results.forecast: Error of the twin's glucose forecasts on real held-out days (median RMSE)
results.fusionSynthetic: Value of combining the data streams, simulated fasting days (AUPRC)
results.fusionReal: Value of combining the data streams, real normal days (AUPRC)
results.parkes: Share of 30-minute forecasts in zones A and B of the Parkes error grid
results.f1: Forecast of low blood sugar during the whole fast, made before the fast (AUROC)

targets.forecast: Lower than the last value at every time
targets.fusion: The full model scores higher than every single data stream

compare.title: Comparison with simpler methods
compare.description: The charts compare the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) for low blood sugar within 60 minutes. AUPRC shows how well a method finds the rare moments before low blood sugar. A higher value is better.

meaning.title: What the results mean
meaning.twinAlone: On simulated fasting days, the twin alone scored a higher AUPRC ({{twin}}) than the full model ({{full}}). The twin also created these simulated days, so this comparison partly favours the twin.
meaning.cgmOnly: On real normal days, the model with CGM data only scored a higher AUPRC ({{cgm}}) than the full model ({{full}}). The real data does not yet show that the smartwatch data adds value.
meaning.falseAlerts: At the alert level that detects 80% of events, the model raised {{value}} false alerts per patient per fasting day, which is more than the target of 2.
meaning.synthetic: The results on simulated fasting days partly reflect the team's modelling assumptions. A clinical study with Indian patients would be needed to confirm them.
